// Raw C# COM-interop fixture. The .txt suffix keeps tooling from treating it as
// real C# source. Named interop attribute, marshal, ProgID, and interop-using
// cases plus a string-literal trap are included. No consumer identifiers and no
// per-application special-casing appear; the Office application name is data.

using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
using static Microsoft.Office.Interop.Excel.XlDirection;
using GenericApp = Microsoft.Office.Interop.Word;

namespace Sample.Interop
{
    // Interop attributes: ComImport, Guid, InterfaceType, DispId.
    [ComImport]
    [Guid("1A2B3C4D-5E6F-7A8B-9C0D-1E2F3A4B5C6D")]
    [InterfaceType(ComInterfaceType.InterfaceIsIUnknown)]
    public interface IGenericComContract
    {
        [DispId(1)]
        void Invoke();
    }

    // ComVisible attribute on a class.
    [ComVisible(true)]
    public class GenericComClass
    {
        public void Release(object comObject)
        {
            // Marshal member calls with different members (no fixed member list).
            Marshal.ReleaseComObject(comObject);
            var count = Marshal.AddRef(IntPtr.Zero);
        }

        public object Activate(string progId)
        {
            // ProgID activation.
            var type = Type.GetTypeFromProgID(progId);
            return Activator.CreateInstance(type);
        }

        public void Trap()
        {
            // Trap: attribute-shaped text inside a string literal must NOT match.
            var pretend = "[Guid(\"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000\")] Marshal.Foo(";
        }
    }
}
